Edit this photograph of a modern house. Keep EVERYTHING exactly as it is - the camera, framing, landscape, sky, light and shadows, the charcoal standing-seam metal roofs and their exact shapes and directions, every pane of glass and every thin black steel frame and post, the patio canopy, the deck and its paving, the black steel platform and legs, all furniture and beds, the floors, the interior walls and the kitchen - and change only these two things:

1. THE FEATURE WALL. The one massive, thick, rust-orange Corten weathering-steel wall that divides the two wings - it runs the full depth of the house, rises a little above both roofs, and is also seen inside through the glass as the rust-colored wall behind the kitchen and behind the beds - becomes a solid wall of warm gray-brown fieldstone laid in neat, roughly squared courses with fine joints. It keeps exactly the same size, thickness, height, outline and position, with crisp square corners. Every face of it - the end faces, the long faces seen through the glass, the inside faces in the rooms, and the part that rises above the roofs - is clad in the same local fieldstone, and its top is finished with a flat, crisp bluestone coping cap. No rust-colored weathering steel remains anywhere on the house. The local fieldstone must be beautifully, precisely laid and catch the same sunlight and shadows as the rest of the scene.

2. THE DOORS, identical in every view of this house. The front door, wherever it appears in the living room's glass wall under the patio canopy, is a single tall 8-foot blackened-steel pivot door with a long vertical black bar pull. Every interior door seen through the glass - bedroom and bathroom doors - is the same tall flush door painted soft white, in a slim white frame, with a slim matte-black lever handle; no wood-toned, gray or paneled doors. Do not add or remove any door, and do not move any; only restyle the doors that are already there.

Completely photorealistic, matching the original photograph's grain, color, exposure and light exactly. No text.
